fatigue.detail: Plain rolled bottom flange; welded attachments are checked separately in the detail register.

notes: Example configuration generated by the CraneCalc configurator; fictitious crane, supplier, site and owner data, to be replaced with project data. Scope: 1 simply supported 35-ft bay, W30X191 girder, one 10-ton cab crane, on new freestanding W14X311 columns with built-up tapered I haunches, base plates, anchor rods and spread footings, and crane-level rod X-bracing; the existing building carries no crane load. Seismic: ordinary steel cantilever column system across the runway and rod bracing not specifically detailed for seismic resistance along it, Seismic Design Category B. The flexible plate cannot pass as sized (tie sizing ratio plate-tie-compression 1.29 > 1.00 for the estimated tie demands): the tie is paired flat bars on the same saddle, each bar taking half the force. A direct flange saddle does not suit this rolled girder (a welded saddle is a Category D/E attachment on the top flange of this high-cycle runway (CMAA Class D, AIST Class C)): the tie is paired flat bars, which bolt to the tie-side bearing stiffener, cut as one plate with its gusset extension past the flange tip (no weld at the gusset), the full-depth stiffener pair carrying the tie force into the girder. Bumper overhang assumed 20 in (end-wheel centerline to the extended bumper face, a typical supplier proportion): the stop contact positions use it; confirm with the crane supplier. The bracket stays: the W10X112 crane-level strut is moment-connected in plan at every column by 0.5 in plates on its flanges (torsion brace, 3 rows of bolt pairs) and holds the new W14X311 columns against the twist: 0.0106 rad factored (limit 0.02) and 0.071 in of bearing movement at every crane start and stop (limit 0.67 in). The strut is sized so the girder's twist movement under the factored traction, 0.114 in, is within 0.125 in (a configurator target, the TR-13 alignment tolerance class, not a code limit). With the strut on the column centerline alone, the girder seated 35.55 in off the column axis, the traction twists the column 0.0942 rad factored (limit 0.02) and 0.63 in of bearing movement at every crane start and stop (limit 0.67 in).

selections.designed: Paired flat bars on a bearing-stiffener gusset
selections.reason: A direct flange saddle does not suit this rolled girder (a welded saddle is a Category D/E attachment on the top flange of this high-cycle runway (CMAA Class D, AIST Class C)): the tie is paired flat bars, which bolt to the tie-side bearing stiffener, cut as one plate with its gusset extension past the flange tip (no weld at the gusset), the full-depth stiffener pair carrying the tie force into the girder.

Lightest compact W within the sizing targets (ratio ≤ 0.85, deflections ≤ 0.9 of the limits): screening estimates, top-flange tip stress (DG7, warping and second-order twist) ratio 0.84, vertical deflection 0.33, lateral 0.57 and rail-head movement with twist 0.81 of their limits; flanges at least 8.5 in wide for the end bearing bolt gauge and the rail seat; lighter candidates rejected: 66 by sizing ratio, 42 by flange width; the next lighter, W40X183: tips ratio 1.62 > 0.85; lateral deflection 1.16 of the limit > 0.9; rail-head movement with twist 1.59 of the limit > 0.9. These are the configurator's screening estimates (a simplified model that ranks the catalog), not the final ratios: the calculation checks the section and reports its own ratios.

New cantilever column for a 10-ton crane (W14X120 to 5 t, W14X159 to 12.5 t, W14X211 to 25 t, else W14X257). The tapered haunch on the W14X159 needs column continuity plates, which clash with the bracing gussets on a new column web: the lightest heavier W14 that needs none; The W14X176 chosen for the crane gives base drift ratio 1.73 > 0.9: the lightest heavier W14 within the drift and torsion ratios.
Set by the tie sizing: the column face moves out from 20 in (to at most 30 in) until the tie passes its imposed-movement and strength checks.

fabrication.steel: Girder ASTM A992; plates, bars and stiffeners ASTM A572 Grade 50 unless noted.
fabrication.bolting: ASTM F3125 Grade A325, pretensioned, Class B faying surfaces, standard holes unless slots are detailed. Sliding-end bearing bolts and column-end tie bolts pretensioned against steel sleeves.
fabrication.welding: E70XX low-hydrogen electrodes per AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020, cyclically loaded provisions. Continuous fillets as dimensioned; no intermittent welds on cyclic load paths. Smooth starts and stops.
fabrication.inspection: Visual inspection of all welds; AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020 cyclically loaded acceptance criteria; magnetic particle testing of fillets at fatigue-sensitive attachments; 100% ultrasonic testing of CJP welds; bolt pretension verification per RCSC.
fabrication.erection: Set and level the bearings, install the end bearings and flange ties, then set the rails. Provide temporary restraint until the permanent ties are complete.
fabrication.railAlignment: Set the rails to the specified gauge, alignment and level tolerances and survey them after erection, before the load test.
